It is important to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: This medication can be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: Your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as cortisol level monitoring, while you are using this medication. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember unless it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature. Do not refrigerate it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Application Instructions: If this product is to be applied inside the anus, use the applicator tip, cap, or nozzle as directed in the product instructions or by your doctor. Fill the applicator with the medication as instructed and insert it approximately 5 centimeters into the anus. Apply the medication in and around the anal opening as directed. Do not use your finger to apply the medication inside the anus. Avoid covering the treated area with plastic or waterproof bandages unless directed by your doctor, as this may increase absorption through the skin. Wash your hands immediately after use and avoid contact with your eyes, nose, ears, or mouth. Dosage: This medication is typically used 2 to 4 times daily, or after each bowel movement, as directed by your doctor. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Do not use more of this product, use it more frequently, or continue using it longer than prescribed by your doctor. If you have been using this medication for an extended period or in high doses, do not stop using it suddenly without your doctor’s approval, as some conditions may worsen when the drug is abruptly discontinued. Side Effects: Common side effects may include redness, burning, or itching at the application site. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, potentially causing side effects associated with excessive corticosteroid levels. These effects are more likely in children and individuals using the medication for prolonged periods. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using this product, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to hydrocortisone or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Prolonged use of corticosteroid medications may make it harder for your body to respond to physical stress. Although unlikely, this medication may temporarily slow a child’s growth if used for an extended period. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary and not for long periods or in large amounts. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This list can be saved and edited at any time. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information, as individual plans may vary and formulary information is subject to change.
